title: Supreme Court Orders Probe Into Police Violence as Rahul Gandhi Escalates Pellet Gun Accountability Push
excerpt: India's top court has formed a panel to investigate allegations of pellet gun use and brutality against student protesters, as the opposition demands FIRs against security personnel.
body:
• India's Supreme Court formed a panel on August 20 to investigate allegations of police violence during student protests that forced Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan to resign last month.
  • Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi has been pressing for FIRs against security personnel, appearing alongside 19-year-old pellet victim Sahil Lochab who faces possible loss of vision.
  • The CRPF has launched a professional review of its Rapid Action Force's actions during the July 20 "Sansad Chalo" march, where at least four protesters suffered confirmed pellet injuries.
  • Delhi Police deny possessing or using pellet guns, but medical records and victim testimonies contradict the official position.

Top Court Intervenes

India's Supreme Court on August 20 created a panel to investigate allegations of police brutality during the student protests that convulsed New Delhi last month, marking the judiciary's most significant intervention in what has become the worst political crisis of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's third term.

https://x.com/ashokdadhwal196/status/2090644968603877599

The panel, headed by a former Supreme Court judge and including two retired judges and two retired police chiefs, will examine claims that security personnel used excessive force — including pellet guns — against demonstrators during the Cockroach Janta Party's "Sansad Chalo" march on July 20, according to Reuters.

The court's order specifically addresses allegations that female protesters faced "targeted violence, harassment, and molestation" and that demonstrators suffered "grievous harm and injury" at the hands of security forces. No deadline was set for the investigation, but the court asked for an interim report as soon as possible.

Gandhi's Campaign for Accountability

Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi has been escalating pressure on the government over the pellet gun issue for weeks. On July 24, Gandhi held a press conference at his residence with Sahil Lochab, a 19-year-old student at Delhi University's School of Open Learning, displaying the student's pellet wounds to reporters.

"The government must stop lying. They have fired guns at the future of India."

— Rahul Gandhi, Leader of the Opposition

Gandhi lifted Lochab's T-shirt to reveal pellet marks on his face, right arm, and upper body. "Pellets hit my brother while he was waving the national flag. He cannot see from his right eye as pellets have hit it. There is uncertainty over whether he will regain his vision," Gandhi told reporters, according to NDTV and India West.

Two days later, Gandhi wrote to Home Minister Amit Shah demanding answers on two specific questions: whether Shah had authorized the use of lethal force including pellet guns on July 20, and whether the plainclothes individuals seen beating protesters were police personnel or civilian volunteers, according to Livemint.

Congress leaders have been pressing for FIRs to be registered against the security personnel responsible for the pellet injuries, staging protests and demanding accountability from senior police officials.

The Evidence Trail

At least four confirmed pellet-injury cases have emerged from the July 20 march. An Outlook journalist also reported being struck by what he believes was a pellet-firing weapon while covering the protest, with hospital records documenting pellet wounds, according to Livemint.

The Hindu reported that 25-year-old Shaikh Irshad Mansoori suffered pellet injuries in what appears to be the first known instance of security forces using pellet guns on civilians in Delhi.

The CRPF has acknowledged that more than 47 RAF personnel were injured in clashes in the Connaught Place area, some seriously, according to Madhyamam. The force has launched a professional review that will examine whether pellet rounds were fired during the march.

"Most shocking has been the use of lethal pellet guns."

— Rahul Gandhi, in letter to Home Minister Amit Shah

Delhi Police have categorically denied the allegations. "Claims stating that Delhi Police forces used pellet guns against peaceful protesters yesterday are completely false and misleading," the force posted on X. "Delhi Police neither possess pellet guns nor do they use them."

The Broader Crisis

The protests were triggered by the leak of question papers for the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET), a nationwide exam that determines access to medical schools. The cancellation of the exam reportedly caused a dozen students to die by suicide and meant that over two million candidates would have to retake the test.

Demonstrations began at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi and spread to other cities. Tens of thousands attempting to march on Parliament were met with tear gas and baton charges. The crisis ended only after Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned.

The International Service for Human Rights has filed a submission with UN Special Rapporteurs, noting that the UN's 2020 Guidance on Less-Lethal Weapons states that metal pellets "should never be used" in the context of civilian assemblies.

What's Next

The government has agreed to examination reforms and compensation for families of students who took their own lives. The Supreme Court panel's findings could determine whether criminal accountability follows for the security personnel involved in the crackdown. The CRPF's internal review is expected to be completed before the panel begins its work, setting the stage for a potential showdown between police accounts and victim testimony.
nri_angle: The student protest movement and police crackdown resonate with Indian diaspora communities concerned about democratic rights and educational integrity in India.
author: Diaspora Desk
